title: Runtime vocabulary/domain learning and Goblin/Millwood knowledge-barrier fixtures

sections.what: Wire runtime learning of foreign vocabulary and domain knowledge into teach, speech context, and examine/read manuals, and author verified character/scenario fixtures exercising word-level language barriers (Goblin/Japanese exchange student) and asymmetrical Millwood domain expertise/ignorance (Sammy, Kayla, Zoe).
sections.why: Static competence sheets go stale quickly unless characters can learn words and craft/trade facts in play, and AGENTS.md rule 8 requires concrete authored fixtures alongside mechanism tests. Extending the existing CraftingSystem.teach command, examine/read grants, and _teach_* hooks avoids inventing new one-off subsystems while proving both target settings end-to-end.
sections.how:
1. Extend CraftingSystem.teach() (engine/crafting.py lines 368-406) and routes/action_handlers.py (lines 1118-1127) to handle lang:<language>:<word_or_phrase> (requiring the teacher to know that language/word and adding it to the student's known_words) and domain:<id> (seeding semantic knowledge and nudging novice familiarity on co-located instruction).
2. Add optional readable-manual / phrasebook grants in engine/items/examine_actions.py and contextual object-pointing word acquisition alongside _teach_names_from_speech/_teach_places_from_speech in engine/speech.py (bounded so strangers cannot bulk-dump whole dictionaries from one overheard monologue).
3. Author concrete reference fixtures across Millwood (data/library/characters/sammy.json, kayla.json, zoe.json: Sammy skateboarding expert vs computing ignorant, Kayla law/language expert vs physics/DIY ignorant, Zoe silicone_molding/DIY expert vs sports ignorant, plus school/parent semantic seeds) and a Goblin/foreign-exchange barrier fixture (e.g. gribba.json plus automated scenario test proving asymmetrical speech masking and runtime word acquisition).
sections.verify:
1. Run pytest covering teach lang:<id>:<word>, teach domain:<id>, examine phrasebook/manual learning, and full Goblin/exchange-student speech masking plus Millwood Sammy/Kayla/Zoe domain asymmetry fixtures.
2. Verify python tools/lint_library.py passes after updating character fixtures.

acceptance.text: teach command (CraftingSystem.teach / routes/action_handlers.py) supports teaching foreign known_words (lang:<id>:<word>) and semantic domain lessons between co-located characters.
Examining/reading authored bilingual phrasebooks, manuals, or pointed single-word object lessons updates listener known_words or semantic memory cleanly.

Millwood character fixtures (Sammy, Kayla, Zoe) and Goblin/bilingual exchange fixtures carry concrete domain competence, explicit ignorant blind spots, and partial known_words verified end-to-end by tests.

custom.browser_ui:
Intended UI home: Human Turn / Agent Turn Composer (teach and read/examine actions), Character Inspector -> Mind -> Persona (Languages & Domains updates at runtime), and Prompt Lens.

Current availability: CraftingSystem.teach in engine/crafting.py (lines 368-406) and routes/action_handlers.py (lines 1118-1127) only accept recipes and skill:<name>, and shipped characters in data/library/characters/ have 0 language lexicons or domain expertise/ignorance profiles.

Manual verification steps:
1. Load Sammy, Kayla, Zoe, or a Goblin/exchange-student pair in a test scenario and inspect Persona Languages/Domains plus Prompt Lens before interaction.
   - expected: Sammy shows skateboarding competence and computing ignorance; Kayla shows legal/language competence and DIY/physics ignorance; Zoe shows silicone_molding/DIY competence and sports ignorance; partial foreign speakers show initial known_words only.
2. Execute 'teach lang:english:silicone to Kenji' (or have Zoe demonstrate/teach DIY curing to Kayla) when co-located.
   - expected: Target character's live known_words or domain/semantic memory updates and persists across save/load, and subsequent WITNESSED speech or examine output reflects the newly learned term.
